Thanks for the call today, Aditya. High level notes from my side:
- We're evaluating Redwood vs our current hyperscaler-managed endpoints and one other inference provider. Primary concerns: per-token cost, latency at 1k context, and reliability for peak daily batch jobs.
- Procurement will need a clear TCO comparison and a sample run (1M tokens simulated) to validate unit economics.
- Security checks look good so far; we may request SOC 2 artifacts.

Next steps I'd like from Redwood:
1) A per-1M token cost breakdown (baseline + with batching/caching assumptions).
2) A short doc comparing where Redwood objectively saves vs hyperscalers (e.g., batching, KV caching, cheaper kernel ops).
3) A proposed test plan for a 1M token simulation and expected metrics you will provide (latency distribution, cost estimate, cache hit rate).

Can you send those in a short email we can share with procurement?

Subject: Re: FinPay: Competitive Eval & Cost Modeling

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear asks and for the time today. Short answers below and attaching a concise TCO workbook and a 2-slide comparison deck for procurement.

1) Per-1M token cost (ballpark)
- Baseline (no batching, no cache): $12.40 / 1M tokens (standard hosted endpoint, medium model family)
- With production tuning (batching + 60% prefix cache hit assumed): $4.80 / 1M tokens
- With Dedicated reserved capacity (committed instance pricing + quantization): ~$2.10 / 1M tokens (at committed utilization >= 70%)

Assumptions are in the attached redwood-tco-1m-tokens.xlsx (tab: assumptions). Important levers: batch size, cache hit rate, request concurrency, and token distribution.

2) Differentiators vs hyperscalers (high level)
- Automatic KV/prefix caching that saves repeated prompt tokens for chat-like workloads (your user prompts + system tokens)
- Continuous batching with latency SLOs (we optimize kernel selection by sequence-length distribution)
- Model variants + quantization guidance that keep quality while reducing GPU cycles
- Policy routing that allows fallbacks to cheaper model variants during peak to preserve availability

3) Proposed 1M token test plan (what we'll deliver)
- Simulate 1M tokens over a day using your sample prompt set (we'll coordinate a sanitized set).
- Provide: per-request latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99), aggregate token cost, achieved cache hit rate, effective batch size distribution, and a small trace sample for failures.
- Timeline: can run the simulation in a dedicated sandbox within 48 hours of signing the test agreement.

Attachments: redwood-tco-1m-tokens.xlsx, redwood-vs-cloud-quick-deck.pdf

Next step: if procurement signs off, can we get a sanitized prompt sample and a procurement contact to send the simple test agreement? I'll loop engineering for the sandbox run.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
